  <span class="subtitle">Hackers :: some reading</span>
  <br><span class="bodytext">
  <br>If you are looking for a good book to help you get started, I can recommend the following books (click on the images for more details and online ordering info at Amazon).
<br>
<table>
<tr>
<td class="bodytext" colspan="2">
If you're new to MIPS, I suggest reading the book 'See MIPS Run' by Dominic Sweetman.
</td><td width="20%">
<A HREF="http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/1558604103/linux4be-20"><IMG SRC="1558604103.01.MZZZZZZZ.gif" border="0" alt="cover" hspace="3" vspace="3"></A>
</td></tr>
<tr><td width="20%"> 
<A HREF="http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/0596000022/linux4be-20"><IMG SRC="0596000022.01.MZZZZZZZ.jpg" border="0" alt="cover" hspace="3" vspace="3"></A>
</td><td class="bodytext" colspan="2">
If you're new to Linux kernel programming, take a look at: Understanding the LINUX Kernel: From I/O Ports to Process Management 
</td></tr>
<tr>
<td class="bodytext" colspan="2">
Linux Device Drivers is a book that John Roark found usefull and is free! Click on the cover image for a link to the pdf download.
</td>
<td width="20%"> 
<A HREF="http://www.xml.com/ldd/chapter/book/"><IMG SRC="linuxdrive2.s.gif" height=140 border="0" alt="Linux Device drivers cover" hspace="3" vspace="3"></A></td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td class="bodytext" colspan="3">
If you're familiar with MIPS, I suggest reading the NEC Manuals for the VR4131 processor. Check the <a href="/hackers/hardware.php">hardware pages</a> for a PDF download.
</td>
</tr>
